name: Miles Davis
hook: A jazz trumpeter who made the best-selling jazz album ever, then plugged in, borrowed from Sly Stone and Stockhausen, and let his producer build albums out of spliced tape.
blurb: Miles Davis was born in Alton, Illinois, on 26 May 1926 and grew up in East St. Louis. He played trumpet in New York's bebop scene from the mid-1940s, and over the next two decades, recording for Prestige and then Columbia, he led some of the most influential small groups in jazz and kept changing his music every few years. 'Kind of Blue' (August 1959) has sold more than five million copies in the US, more than any other jazz album. At the end of the 1960s he started using electric instruments and rock and funk rhythms. 'Bitches Brew' (recorded August 1969, released March 1970) and 'On the Corner' (recorded mid-1972) were put together by his producer, Teo Macero, from hours of studio jams: he cut the tapes into pieces, joined them back together and added tape loops, delays and echo afterwards, which is close to how sampling and editing work today. The title track of 'Bitches Brew' has fifteen edits. Paul Buckmaster introduced Davis to the composer Karlheinz Stockhausen's music in 1972, and Davis described 'On the Corner' as Stockhausen plus funk plus Ornette Coleman, with Sly Stone and James Brown audible in the bass and drums. It sold poorly and many jazz fans hated it. It is now credited as an ancestor of hip-hop, drum and bass and electronica, though that view was mostly formed looking back. Ill health kept him from performing from 1975 to 1980. He recorded for Warner Bros. from 1986 and died in Santa Monica on 28 September 1991.

signatureTracks.title: So What
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The first track on 'Kind of Blue': a tune built on two scales instead of a run of chords.

signatureTracks.title: Pharaoh's Dance
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: From 'Bitches Brew', with nineteen tape edits: a piece made in the editing as much as in the playing.

signatureTracks.title: On the Corner
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Funk bass and drums looping under wah-wah trumpet: his own 'Stockhausen plus funk'.
